name: ANSSI (regles cryptographiques)
edition: ANSSI-PG-083 v3.00 (2026-03-20), with ANSSI-PA-079 v1.0 and DAT-NT-007 v1.3
reference: ANSSI-PG-083 'Regles et recommandations concernant le choix et le dimensionnement des mecanismes cryptographiques' v3.00; algorithm status from ANSSI-PA-079 'Guide de selection d'algorithmes cryptographiques' v1.0; SSH specifics from DAT-NT-007 'Recommandations pour un usage securise d'(Open)SSH' v1.3.
summary: The French baseline. ANSSI publishes cryptographic rules by mechanism and parameter, not SSH algorithm lists, so this profile encodes the rules rather than inventing a configuration.
notes: ANSSI distinguishes 'regles' (mandatory for conformance) from 'recommandations' (not formally required); this profile enforces the regles and reports the recommandations here. It deliberately sets no single minimum security strength, because PG-083 section 1.5 states ANSSI publishes no summary table of minimum sizes on purpose: the rules are stated per mechanism, and collapsing them into one figure would be our synthesis rather than ANSSI's rule. That is why an RSA-2048 host key passes here while failing BSI and ENS. The regle for RSA and finite-field Diffie-Hellman is 2048 bits for use up to the end of 2030 and 3072 bits from 2031, while 3072 bits today is a recommandation. Three points people get wrong: ChaCha20-Poly1305 is explicitly recommended by ANSSI, not merely tolerated, so rejecting it in ANSSI's name would be incorrect; ANSSI publishes no KexAlgorithms or HostKeyAlgorithms list in any document, so any such list would be derived rather than cited; and CBC is excluded here on the authority of DAT-NT-007 rule R15, which mandates CTR mode for SSH, not on the authority of the crypto guide, which does permit CBC in general. HMAC-SHA-1 is a genuine conflict in ANSSI's own corpus: DAT-NT-007 R15 (2015) allows it and the selection guide tolerates it, but PG-083 v3.00 requires the underlying primitive to be conformant and lists SHA-1 as non-conformant. This profile follows the current crypto guide and rejects it. On post-quantum, ANSSI-FT-116 (February 2026) states hybridisation is the preferred route and is mandatory for the first two phases of its roadmap, which is the opposite of CNSA 2.0's standalone ML-KEM-1024 requirement.

host_key.reason: PG-083 v3.00 lists SHA-1 as non-conformant to RegleHachage.1 and RegleHachage.2, so SHA-1 signatures cannot be conformant. DAT-NT-007 also requires DSA host keys to be removed.

cipher.reason: DAT-NT-007 rule R15 mandates AES in CTR mode for SSH: 'Le mode CTR permet de s'affranchir de vulnerabilites connues du mode CBC tel qu'utilise par SSH.' Two-key and three-key Triple DES are both listed as non-conformant by PG-083.

mac.reason: PG-083 v3.00 RegleMAC.1 requires the underlying primitive to be conformant, and SHA-1 is not. Tags must be at least 96 bits, and 128 bits is recommended.

kex.reason: SHA-1 is non-conformant, and 1024-bit groups fall below the minimum. Standalone post-quantum key establishment is excluded because ANSSI-FT-116 requires hybridisation with a classical mechanism during the current transition phases.
